title: Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency: First Re-Charged Day after Medicare Part A Liability Ends
content:
**Medicare liaison guidance — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.** If the other payer source is denied or ends while the resident stays, private-pay billing resumes: after a Medicaid denial, the denied pending period is charged again at the private rate from the original conversion date; after Part A coverage ends, from the day after the last covered date, save that a late SNF Advance Beneficiary Notice moves the first re-charged day and a pending expedited review holds every day, as set out here; only the re-charge span on the agreement's latest advance does so, and every other resumption stays under the base rule.

**Records read.** From the resident's **Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage** records: the episode whose booked days run latest, its booked block that begins latest deciding; that episode's last covered date and status; and the SNF Advance Beneficiary Notice most recently delivered for that episode.

**How the re-charge days start.**
- **Late notice.** Where an SNF Advance Beneficiary Notice on file describes care from a day after the Part A last covered date, was delivered after the first day of the care it describes, and records option 1 or option 2, the first re-charged day is the notice's delivery date, that day counted, the center bearing the days before it.
- **Review pending.** Where no such notice is on file and an expedited review of the episode is pending, no day is re-charged, the resident not being billed while the review is pending.
- **Otherwise.** The re-charge days start on the conversion date recorded on the agreement when private-pay billing resumed, that day counted.

**Points of judgement.** A notice delivered on the very day the care it describes began was not delivered after that day, so it does not move the first re-charged day. A notice recording option 3 does not either. No such notice and the episode under expedited review: nothing is re-charged while the review is pending.
